walkthroughs.body_html:
Everything that begins to exist has a cause.

Aquinas: an infinite chain of causes is impossible, so there must be a first cause — God.

The modern Kalam version: the universe began (Big Bang), so it has a cause beyond itself.

The universe looks designed.

Paley (1802): find a watch on a heath, you'd know it had a maker. The world is far more complex, so it must have a Designer.

Modern: fine-tuning — the laws of physics seem precisely set for life.

Religious experience: direct encounter — visions, conversion (St Paul, road to Damascus), the numinous (awe, Rudolf Otto), answered prayer.

Miracles break natural law — Jesus' healings, Lourdes cures.

For believers, these are evidence of God. Hume objected: miracles are always less likely than mistaken witnesses.

mcqs.q: Is the Buddha a god in Buddhism?
options: No — the Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama) is regarded as an enlightened human teacher who discovered the path to liberation. Theravada Buddhism is generally non-theistic; some Mahayana traditions develop more elaborate cosmologies.
The Buddha created the universe.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
Buddhists worship the Buddha as their god.
